title: The flash photo showed someone in front of me 📸
style_prompt: cinematic horror film still, dark moody blue-teal grade, one bright light source, well exposed, 35mm film grain, realistic, no text, no watermark, no faces
hook_text: At 12:48 a.m. my flash photo showed someone standing in front of me.

scenes.narration: At 12:48 a.m. my flash photo showed someone standing in front of me.
I was texting in bed with the lights off. I tapped the wrong button. The flash went off. I thought nothing of it.

shots.prompt: phone on a dark bed with a bright white glare, no face

scenes.narration: Then I saw the picture. My room. My wardrobe. My own feet at the bottom of the frame.

shots.prompt: phone screen showing a dim photo of a bedroom, bright glare, no text, no face

scenes.narration: And between the bed and the camera, close enough to touch, someone was standing. Facing me. Absolutely still.

shots.prompt: dim flash photo of a dark room with a pale blurry figure close to the camera, no face, fully clothed

scenes.narration: I looked up. The room was empty. I lifted the phone and took another picture. Flash. Click.

shots.prompt: dark empty bedroom lit by a camera flash, no person

scenes.narration: The figure was closer. Now it was leaning over the bed. Its head was tilted to look at the screen of my phone.

shots.prompt: flash photo of a dark bedroom with a tall blurry silhouette bending over the bed, no face, fully clothed

scenes.narration: I took a third picture, because I needed to see. Flash. In the photo, there was nobody behind me anymore.

shots.prompt: bright flash on a bedroom wall, empty bed, no person

scenes.narration: That is when I understood where it had gone. The phone was in my hand. My thumb was not on the button.

shots.prompt: phone in a dark room, screen showing a flash icon, no text, no face

scenes.narration: So tell me. Do you take one more photo, or put the phone down?
